Purpose and exclusions

Walk/East visual placeholder or later audited clip.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Create a Flipbook only after its sprites have explicit audited frame rectangles or legal debug frames. Assign ordered frames and duration from the source guide when available.
  2. For missing action/facing use DA_AnimationSet_Common explicit fallback, not an invented diagonal or mirrored asymmetric weapon.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Author and validate stable definition/frame/field identity before use; load through declared references at readiness.
  2. Consumers may cache read-only references for their world/session lifetime; do not mutate the shared definition or place player quantities on it.
  3. On reimport/version change validate compatibility and migrate persistent IDs deliberately. Missing required rules fail closed; missing cosmetic layers use documented fallback.
  4. World/pawn teardown releases runtime references; persistent records retain IDs and versions only. Reconnect resolves the same definition without replaying grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Layered sprites, facing, appearance and remote avatars. Rule owner: URPGPaperDollComponent. This asset’s role is Walk/East visual placeholder or later audited clip.

  1. Owning movement/combat/gather components publish a semantic action and accepted timestamp; the server does not send each PNG frame.
  2. URPGPaperDollComponent resolves matching body and gear pages before starting playback. Missing gear may hide that layer but cannot alter equipped stats.
  3. A single PaperZD animation driver selects the body sequence. The project adapter reads its effective frame/normalized time and drives compatible overlays from that same clock.
  4. Facing is derived from movement or action aim in the camera-ground basis with hysteresis; use a four-direction lookup, not diagonal art invented by mirroring.
  5. Remote clients use replicated action sequence/timestamp plus interpolated movement. Late packets skip to the current pose or finish harmlessly; they do not replay gameplay.
  6. On a camera elevation/floor change, keep the capsule and foot anchor in world space. Nameplates and portraits use safe identity/appearance snapshots, never account IDs.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_ArtLab / Avatar_A / Avatar_B / OutfitProbe. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Outfit page p1 assigned during a pBOW action -> PageMismatch warning and explicit fallback; no shifted limbs.
Body clip missing -> MissingBody diagnostic silhouette; gameplay remains functional in a development lab.
Missing animation notify -> accepted hit/reward and action completion still occur from the authority.
Duplicate action sequence -> no duplicate sound or visual spawn; stale appearance revision ignored.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
